note: zzip_mem_entry_extra_block() (zzip/memdisk.c) walks the heap-allocated copy of a zip central-directory entry's "extra data" field with while (*(short*)(ext->z_datatype)), advancing its cursor on every iteration by the block's own attacker-controlled datasize field (e += zzip_extra_block_get_datasize(ext)) with no comparison against any captured end-of-buffer pointer anywhere in the function. The extra data was copied into a malloc(ext1 + 2)-sized buffer whose last two bytes act as a zero sentinel meant to terminate the loop -- but a crafted datasize can skip the cursor straight past that sentinel, so the next iteration's ext->z_datatype read runs off the end of the heap allocation.

traces.message: while (*(short *) (ext->z_datatype)) : loop condition dereferences the cursor with no bound on how far it has advanced
e += zzip_extra_block_get_datasize(ext) : cursor advanced by the block's own untrusted datasize field, no comparison against any end-of-buffer pointer
ext = (void *) e : next iteration's z_datatype dereference can now be past the end of the malloc(ext1 + 2)/malloc(ext2 + 2) heap allocation
